column1: It ate the desk, skapi. One screen, so the output took all of it. I put it in a little window, behind. A real show gets a second screen.
column2: Ua ʻai ia i ka papa, skapi. Hoʻokahi papakaumaka, no laila ua lawe ka puka i nā mea a pau. Ua waiho au iā ia ma kahi puka aniani liʻiliʻi, ma hope. Loaʻa i ka hōʻike maoli he papakaumaka ʻelua.
UA ʻAI IA I KA PAPA

column1: There. The button that says OUTPUT OFF. Make it say ON, skapi.
column2: Aia. Ka pihi e ʻōlelo ana OUTPUT OFF. E hoʻololi iā ia i ON, skapi.

column1: Nothing is live to fade from, skapi. TAKE one cue first, then pick the other and give it a time.
column2: ʻAʻohe mea ola e hala mai ai, skapi. TAKE mua i hoʻokahi cue, a laila koho i kekahi a hāʻawi i ka manawa.

column1: That was a cut, skapi. Fast, but not a crossfade. Pick the other cue, press + on transition, then TAKE.
column2: He ʻoki kēlā, skapi. Wikiwiki, akā ʻaʻole he crossfade. Koho i ka cue ʻē aʻe, kaomi i ka + ma transition, a laila TAKE.

column1: A feedback loop! Output patched straight back into the desk. Happens to the best of us. Mostly to me. 1983. We don't talk about 1983.
column2: He pōʻai hoʻihoʻi! Ua patch pololei ʻia ka puka i ka papa. Hiki i nā mea maikaʻi loa. Iaʻu ka hapa nui. 1983. ʻAʻole kāua e kamaʻilio no 1983.

column1: No more rakia. The rat has a problem.
column2: ʻAʻohe rakia hou. He pilikia ko ka ʻiole.

column1: Nazdrave, skapi! Baba's rakia, from Belogradchik. One glass, for the lesson.
column2: Nazdrave, skapi! Ka rakia a Baba, mai Belogradchik. Hoʻokahi kīʻaha, no ka haʻawina.

column1: Is this... is this allowed during a tutorial?
column2: ʻAe ʻia anei... ʻae ʻia anei kēia i ka wā o ka haʻawina?
*hoʻoluliluli i ke poʻo* ʻO ka hoʻokahi hou kēlā.

column1: I love you all. I love the oscillator. I love the OUTPUT. It's video. I know. I KNOW.
column2: Aloha au iā ʻoukou a pau. Aloha au i ka oscillator. Aloha au i ka OUTPUT. He wikiō ia. ʻIke au. ʻIKE AU.

column1: ...and the rat took the rakia. Every time, skapi. Every single time.
column2: ...a lawe ka ʻiole i ka rakia. I kēlā me kēia manawa, skapi. I kēlā me kēia manawa.

column1: Was that a rat? In a hat? With a pizza?
column2: He ʻiole anei kēlā? Me ka pāpale? Me ka pizza?

column1: Stop that. I am a serious man.
column2: Hoʻōki i kēlā. He kanaka koʻikoʻi au.

column1: Do not tell Dr. Pixel about this.
column2: Mai haʻi iā Dr. Pixel no kēia.

column1: This never happened. Back to the patch bay.
column2: ʻAʻole i hana ʻia kēia. Hoʻi i ka papa patch.

column1: It was the eighties. Everyone had a bow tie.
column2: ʻO nā makahiki kanawalu ia. He kāʻei ʻāʻī pewa ko nā kānaka a pau.
Ka lawe ʻana i ke alanui

column1: CHECK a show before it travels, fix what it finds, and bundle it with its media.
column2: CHECK i ka hōʻike ma mua o kona huakaʻi, hoʻoponopono i nā mea i loaʻa, a hoʻopūʻolo me kāna media.
Nā hopena, nā oscillator a me ka waihoʻoluʻu

column1: An effect, a ~ on its knob, and the colour picker.
column2: He hopena, he ~ ma kona pihi, a me ka mea koho waihoʻoluʻu.

column1: The art school crit, with Mr. Salty
column2: Ka loiloi kula noʻeau, me Mr. Salty
Nā kāpoʻe, nā synth a me ke kaha kiʻi

column1: A test pattern, the video synth, and drawing on the picture, saved as a still.
column2: He kāpoʻe hoʻāʻo, ka synth wikiō, a me ke kaha kiʻi ma luna o ke kiʻi, mālama ʻia ma ke ʻano he kiʻi paʻa.

column1: The telestrator booth, with Coach Marv
column2: Ka lumi telestrator, me Coach Marv

column1: A heart from the library, the pen, invert and feather.
column2: He puʻuwai mai ka waihona, ka peni, ka hoʻohuli a me ka hulu.

column1: The Signal Files: redact the evidence
column2: The Signal Files: hūnā i ka hōʻike
Hoʻokekeʻe, hoʻohui a me nā ʻāpana

column1: A corner pin, two soft edges, then three slices in the Screens window.
column2: He kihi i hoʻopaʻa ʻia, ʻelua ʻaoʻao palupalu, a laila ʻekolu ʻāpana ma ka puka aniani Screens.

column1: The haunted lighthouse, with Keeper Rook
column2: Ka hale ipukukui lapu, me Keeper Rook
GO mai nā wahi a pau

column1: Cue numbers, GOTO, a hotkey, and where Companion, MIDI and OSC come in.
column2: Nā helu cue, GOTO, he kī wikiwiki, a me kahi e komo mai ai ʻo Companion, MIDI a me OSC.

column1: The game show, with Donna Wheel
column2: Ka hōʻike pāʻani, me Donna Wheel

column1: A Lower Third with a name on it, then a title card with a key-green backdrop.
column2: He Lower Third me ka inoa, a laila he kāleka poʻo inoa me ke kua ʻōmaʻomaʻo kī.

column1: The kaiju weather report, with June O'Neil
column2: Ka wānana ʻeā kaiju, me June O'Neil
Ka mālama ʻana i ka manawa

column1: A stage timer counting down, held, and a presenter view for the person on stage.
column2: He uaki kahua e helu ana i lalo, paʻa ʻia, a me ka nānā o ka mea hōʻike no ke kanaka ma ke kahua.

column1: A grand day out, with Wallis and Grommet
column2: He lā nui ma waho, me Wallis lāua ʻo Grommet
ʻElua papa helu a me TAKE ALL

column1: A second playlist as a layer, and TAKE ALL so two things change on one beat.
column2: He papa helu ʻelua ma ke ʻano he papa, a me TAKE ALL i loli ʻelua mea i ka paʻi hoʻokahi.

column1: The magic show, with Turnip Top
column2: Ka hōʻike kilokilo, me Turnip Top

column1: BLACK against PANIC, and getting a show back.
column2: BLACK kūʻē iā PANIC, a me ka hoʻihoʻi ʻana i ka hōʻike.

column1: The cooking show, with Chef Bork
column2: Ka hōʻike kuke, me Chef Bork

column1: Capture a look on a DASH button, change everything, and get it back with one press.
column2: Hopu i ke ʻano ma kekahi pihi DASH, hoʻololi i nā mea a pau, a hoʻihoʻi me ke kaomi hoʻokahi.

column1: The styles beyond the crossfade: an iris, a shatter, and their times.
column2: Nā ʻano ma waho o ka crossfade: he iris, he shatter, a me ko lāua mau manawa.

column1: The space-opera trailer, with Optimus Primetime
column2: Ka hōʻike mua kiʻiʻoniʻoni ākea, me Optimus Primetime

column1: An audio effect on a cue, a bend that damages it beautifully, and where the patch lives.
column2: He hopena leo ma ka cue, he kekeʻe e hōʻino nani ana iā ia, a me kahi e noho ai ka patch.

column1: The robot DJs, with Deft Funk
column2: Nā DJ lopako, me Deft Funk
Ka heluhelu ʻana i nā scope

column1: The waveform, the vectorscope, and false colour: is the glow real, or just too bright?
column2: Ka waveform, ka vectorscope, a me ka waihoʻoluʻu wahaheʻe: he ʻoiaʻiʻo anei ka ʻōlinolino, a i ʻole he ʻōlinolino loa wale nō?

column1: The Signal Files: is the glow on the horizon a craft?
column2: The Signal Files: he moku anei ka ʻōlinolino ma ka ʻalihi lani?

column1: Where NDI, SDI and ST 2110 live, and NDI switched on where this computer has it.
column2: Kahi e noho ai ʻo NDI, SDI a me ST 2110, a me ka hoʻā ʻana i ka NDI ma kahi i loaʻa iā ia ma kēia kamepiula.

column1: The webcam as a controller, as a game. Five rounds, a high score.
column2: Ka pahupaʻikiʻi pūnaewele ma ke ʻano he mea kāohi, ma ke ʻano he pāʻani. ʻElima puni, he helu kiʻekiʻe.
He mea lima, a me nā ʻelala

column1: Windows, the ... menu, what each one shows, layouts, and tally.
column2: Nā puka aniani, ka papa ..., ka mea e hōʻike ai kēlā me kēia, nā hoʻonohonoho, a me ka tally.

column1: Mystery on the starship Cathode, with Lt. Haila and Ensign Jinkley
column2: Pohihihi ma ka moku hōkū Cathode, me Lt. Haila lāua ʻo Ensign Jinkley

column1: DR. PIXEL: Two playlists: Deckboy becomes SUPER DECKBOY. It earned it, skapi.
column2: DR. PIXEL: ʻElua papa helu: lilo ʻo Deckboy i SUPER DECKBOY. Ua loaʻa pono iā ia, skapi.

column1: PROF. VIDEO: It evolved! My oscillators never got a fanfare.
column2: PROF. VIDEO: Ua ulu ia! ʻAʻohe pū hoʻolauleʻa i koʻu mau oscillator.

column1: DR. PIXEL: SUPER DECKBOY! Every show deserves one. Bravo.
column2: DR. PIXEL: SUPER DECKBOY! Pono ka hōʻike a pau i hoʻokahi. Bravo.

column1: PROF. VIDEO: The power-up! More playlists, more layers, more super.
column2: PROF. VIDEO: Ka hoʻoikaika! Nui aʻe nā papa helu, nui aʻe nā papa, nui aʻe ka super.

column1: Intro video (left on the office PC)
column2: Wikiō hoʻomaka (waiho ʻia ma ka kamepiula keʻena)

column1: A show you built here, skapi, running on a laptop somewhere else tonight. Press START.
column2: He hōʻike āu i kūkulu ai ma ʻaneʻi, skapi, e holo ana ma kahi kamepiula lawelima ma kahi ʻē i kēia pō. Kaomi i START.

column1: Before it travels: check it, fix it, bundle it.
column2: Ma mua o kona huakaʻi: nānā, hoʻoponopono, hoʻopūʻolo.

column1: See CHECK in the top bar? It only appears when something is wrong. Press it.
column2: ʻIke ʻoe i ka CHECK ma ka pae luna? Puka mai ia ke hewa kekahi mea. Kaomi iā ia.

column1: It lists everything a show would trip over: missing files, empty cues, unreachable outputs.
column2: Helu ia i nā mea a pau e hina ai ka hōʻike: nā waihona nalo, nā cue nele, nā puka hiki ʻole ke hōʻea.

column1: The intro video is on another computer. Select it and delete it, or RELINK it if you have the file.
column2: Aia ka wikiō hoʻomaka ma kekahi kamepiula ʻē aʻe. Koho iā ia a holoi, a i ʻole RELINK inā loaʻa iā ʻoe ka waihona.

column1: Fix it at home, where it is easy. Not at the venue, where it is not.
column2: E hoʻoponopono ma ka home, kahi maʻalahi. ʻAʻole ma ke kahua, kahi paʻakikī.

column1: Press BUNDLE and choose where: a USB stick, a shared folder. The show and all its media, together.
column2: Kaomi i BUNDLE a koho i kahi: he USB, he waihona kaʻana. Ka hōʻike a me kāna media a pau, pū.

column1: The copy finds its media beside it, wherever the folder goes.
column2: Loaʻa i ke kope kāna media ma kona ʻaoʻao, i kahi e hele ai ka waihona.

column1: Checked, fixed, bundled. On the other machine, open the bundle's show: everything is where it should be.
column2: Nānā ʻia, hoʻoponopono ʻia, hoʻopūʻolo ʻia. Ma ka kamepiula ʻē aʻe, wehe i ka hōʻike o ka pūʻolo: aia nā mea a pau ma ko lākou wahi.

column1: A show file is only text, so it travels light. The media is the heavy part.
column2: He huaʻōlelo wale nō ka waihona hōʻike, no laila māmā kona huakaʻi. ʻO ka media ka ʻāpana kaumaha.

column1: An art school, skapi. One student, one picture, one critic who has seen it all. Press START.
column2: He kula noʻeau, skapi. Hoʻokahi haumāna, hoʻokahi kiʻi, hoʻokahi mea loiloi i ʻike i nā mea a pau. Kaomi i START.

column1: Effects change a picture; an oscillator keeps changing it. The critic only likes the second kind.
column2: Hoʻololi nā hopena i ke kiʻi; hoʻololi mau ka oscillator. ʻO ke ʻano ʻelua wale nō ka makemake o ka mea loiloi.

column1: A grey square on beige. I have seen this at every graduate show since 1987.
column2: He huinahā hina ma luna o ka ʻulaʻula ʻeleʻele māmā. Ua ʻike au i kēia ma kēlā me kēia hōʻike puka kula mai 1987.

column1: In the inspector's EFFECTS section, + adds one. Edges is a good start: it draws the outlines.
column2: Ma ka ʻāpana EFFECTS o ka nānā cue, hoʻohui ka + i hoʻokahi. He hoʻomaka maikaʻi ʻo Edges: kaha ia i nā laina waho.

column1: There are dozens. Every one runs on the CPU in a few milliseconds. Mostly.
column2: He nui loa. Holo kēlā me kēia ma ka CPU i kekahi mau millisecond. Ka hapa nui.

column1: Take a risk! Bad art is fine. Boring art is a crime.
column2: E hoʻāʻo! Maikaʻi ke kiʻi ʻino. He hewa ke kiʻi hoʻoluhi.

column1: Every control with a ~ beside it can follow an oscillator. Press one. The knob starts to breathe.
column2: Hiki i nā mana a pau me ka ~ ma ka ʻaoʻao ke hahai i ka oscillator. Kaomi i hoʻokahi. Hoʻomaka ka pihi e hanu.

column1: A low-frequency oscillator: slow, so the eye can follow it. A quarter of a hertz is a four-second breath.
column2: He oscillator alapine haʻahaʻa: lohi, i hiki i ka maka ke hahai. He hapahā hertz he hanu ʻehā kekona.

column1: Now it MOVES. Okay. Okay. I'm listening.
column2: I kēia manawa NEʻE ia. ʻAe. ʻAe. Ke hoʻolohe nei au.

column1: Effects that draw a colour, like Edges' line, have a colour chip. It opens the picker: a wheel, typed names, or a colour off the screen.
column2: He pahu waihoʻoluʻu ko nā hopena e kaha ana i ka waihoʻoluʻu, e like me ka laina o Edges. Wehe ia i ka mea koho: he huila, nā inoa i kikokiko ʻia, a i ʻole he waihoʻoluʻu mai ka papakaumaka.

column1: Every colour has a name somewhere. Mine is 'oscilloscope green'. Nobody else uses it.
column2: He inoa ko kēlā me kēia waihoʻoluʻu ma kekahi wahi. ʻO koʻu ʻo 'ʻōmaʻomaʻo oscilloscope'. ʻAʻohe mea ʻē aʻe e hoʻohana.

column1: That colour is doing something. I don't know what. I love it.
column2: Ke hana nei kēlā waihoʻoluʻu i kekahi mea. ʻAʻole au i ʻike i ka mea. Aloha au iā ia.

column1: An effect, a ~ and a colour. The critic is crying, skapi. Good crying, I think.
column2: He hopena, he ~ a me ka waihoʻoluʻu. Ke uē nei ka mea loiloi, skapi. Uē maikaʻi, manaʻo wau.

column1: Stack a few. Each has its own ~ on every knob. That is how a look becomes a performance.
column2: Hōʻuluʻulu i kekahi. He ~ ponoʻī ko kēlā me kēia pihi. Pēlā e lilo ai ke ʻano i hōʻike.

column1: It's still a square. But it's YOUR square. Post it.
column2: He huinahā nō. Akā ʻo KĀU huinahā. Kau iā ia.

column1: Coach Marv explains sport by drawing circles on it. Once he circled the sun. Ten minutes, skapi.
column2: Wehewehe ʻo Coach Marv i ka haʻuki ma ke kaha ʻana i nā pōʻai ma luna. Ua kaha pōʻai ʻo ia i ka lā i kekahi manawa. ʻUmi minuke, skapi.

column1: Tonight: test patterns, the video synth, and drawing on the picture. Press START.
column2: I kēia pō: nā kāpoʻe hoʻāʻo, ka synth wikiō, a me ke kaha kiʻi ma luna o ke kiʻi. Kaomi i START.

column1: Get me a picture and a pen. BOOM.
column2: Hāʻawi mai i ke kiʻi a me ka peni. BOOM.

column1: Line up the screens BEFORE the show. Not during. I learned this in Plovdiv.
column2: Hoʻonohonoho i nā papakaumaka MA MUA o ka hōʻike. ʻAʻole i loko. Ua aʻo au i kēia ma Plovdiv.

column1: Every desk needs a test pattern. PATTERN adds Pocket Test: checked against real meters.
column2: Pono kēlā me kēia papa i ke kāpoʻe hoʻāʻo. Hoʻohui ʻo PATTERN i ka Pocket Test: nānā ʻia me nā mika maoli.

column1: He says 'no camera needed' like it is a feature. It is a feature.
column2: ʻŌlelo ʻo ia 'ʻaʻohe pahupaʻikiʻi e pono ai' me he mea lā he mea maikaʻi ia. He mea maikaʻi nō.

column1: My favourite. SOURCE, then Video Synth: oscillators, mirrors and feedback. No camera needed.
column2: Kaʻu punahele. SOURCE, a laila Video Synth: nā oscillator, nā aniani a me ka hoʻihoʻi. ʻAʻohe pahupaʻikiʻi e pono ai.

column1: Select it, then TAKE. Confident operators press Enter.
column2: Koho iā ia, a laila TAKE. Kaomi ka poʻe paʻa i ka Enter.

column1: That's our replay. Every replay needs a pundit.
column2: ʻO kā kākou hana hou kēlā. Pono kēlā me kēia hana hou i ka mea wehewehe.

column1: Now here's a replay. And here's a guy. And BOOM, he's in it.
column2: Eia ka hana hou. A eia kekahi kanaka. A BOOM, aia ʻo ia i loko.

column1: Ink goes on top, on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Hele ka ʻīnika ma luna, ma kona papa ponoʻī. Kaomi i ka + ma ka hopena o nā kāwele papa helu.

column1: A second playlist is a layer over the first. Like a second oscillator, mixed on top.
column2: He papa ma luna o ka mua ka papa helu ʻelua. E like me ka oscillator ʻelua, hui ʻia ma luna.

column1: In the new playlist: SOURCE, then Draw. Clear everywhere you have not drawn.
column2: Ma ka papa helu hou: SOURCE, a laila Draw. Akaka i nā wahi a pau āu i kaha ʻole ai.

column1: A Draw cue is transparent outside the ink, so the synth shows through.
column2: Akaka ka cue Draw ma waho o ka ʻīnika, no laila ʻike ʻia ka synth ma lalo.

column1: Select the Draw cue and TAKE it. Two playlists, two layers, one picture.
column2: Koho i ka cue Draw a TAKE iā ia. ʻElua papa helu, ʻelua papa, hoʻokahi kiʻi.

column1: Now both are live: the synth underneath, the ink on top.
column2: Ola lāua ʻelua i kēia manawa: ka synth ma lalo, ka ʻīnika ma luna.

column1: Press DRAW in the inspector, then draw on the programme monitor. Mouse, or a pen if you have one.
column2: Kaomi i DRAW ma ka nānā cue, a laila kaha ma ka papakaumaka papahana. ʻIole, a i ʻole peni inā loaʻa.

column1: A pen's pressure makes the line thicker. A mouse presses at one strength. Like me.
column2: Hoʻomānoanoa ke kaomi ʻana o ka peni i ka laina. Kaomi ka ʻiole me ka ikaika hoʻokahi. E like me aʻu.

column1: Circle him! No, bigger. BOOM. That's a cloud. Fine. Circle the cloud.
column2: Kaha pōʻai iā ia! ʻAʻole, nui aʻe. BOOM. He ao kēlā. ʻAe. Kaha pōʻai i ke ao.
E MĀLAMA I KE KIʻI PAʻA

column1: SAVE STILL keeps the drawing as a picture with a clear background, and adds it to the playlist.
column2: Mālama ʻo SAVE STILL i ke kaha ma ke ʻano he kiʻi me ke kua akaka, a hoʻohui iā ia i ka papa helu.

column1: For next week's show. Coach Marv will want the cloud again.
column2: No ka hōʻike o kēlā pule aku. Makemake ʻo Coach Marv i ke ao hou.

column1: Patterns, the synth, a layer, ink, a still. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: Nā kāpoʻe, ka synth, he papa, ka ʻīnika, he kiʻi paʻa. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: Try Replay in the Draw section: it draws your lines back the way you drew them.
column2: E hoʻāʻo i ka Replay ma ka ʻāpana Draw: kaha hou ia i kāu mau laina e like me kāu i kaha ai.

column1: Same time next week. Bring a bigger pen. And a turducken.
column2: Ka manawa like i kēlā pule aku. Lawe mai i peni nui aʻe. A me ka turducken.

column1: The Bureau of Unexplained Signals. Two agents, one photo, and it must not air. Press START.
column2: Ke Keʻena o nā Hōʻailona Hoʻomaopopo ʻole ʻia. ʻElua ʻelele, hoʻokahi kiʻi, a ʻaʻole pono e hoʻolele ʻia. Kaomi i START.

column1: Masks cut a picture into shapes. Tonight we cut evidence.
column2: ʻOki nā uhi i ke kiʻi i nā kinona. I kēia pō ʻoki kākou i ka hōʻike.

column1: That's a craft, Brandt. Look at the lights. I want to believe.
column2: He moku kēlā, Brandt. E nānā i nā kukui. Makemake au e manaʻoʻiʻo.

column1: In the inspector's MASK section: mask, then 'new heart'. Any shape will do. The heart is funnier.
column2: Ma ka ʻāpana MASK o ka nānā cue: mask, a laila 'new heart'. Maikaʻi kekahi kinona. ʻAkaʻaka aʻe ka puʻuwai.

column1: The library has circles, stars, hearts. Each one is points you can move.
column2: He mau pōʻai, nā hōkū, nā puʻuwai ma ka waihona. He mau kiko ko kēlā me kēia hiki iā ʻoe ke neʻe.

column1: A heart, Hollis? The Bureau redacts with black bars.
column2: He puʻuwai, Hollis? Hūnā ke Keʻena me nā kaola ʻeleʻele.

column1: Set the tool to pen, then click round the saucer on the monitor. Click the first point to close it.
column2: Hoʻonoho i ka mea hana i ka peni, a laila kaomi a puni ka pā lele ma ka papakaumaka. Kaomi i ke kiko mua e pani.

column1: Click for corners, drag for curves. The way the Bezier brothers intended.
column2: Kaomi no nā kihi, kauo no nā pihi. E like me ka manaʻo o nā kaikunāne Bezier.

column1: Draw round it carefully. It might be watching.
column2: Kaha a puni me ka mālama. Ke nānā mai nei paha ia.

column1: Invert keeps the outside and cuts the inside. The saucer goes. The sky stays.
column2: Mālama ʻo Invert i waho a ʻoki i loko. Hala ka pā lele. Noho ka lani.

column1: The same shape, the other way round. Very useful. Slightly spooky.
column2: Ka kinona like, ma ka ʻaoʻao ʻē. Pono loa. Weliweli iki.

column1: Hollis, there's a heart-shaped hole in the sky.
column2: Hollis, he lua kinona puʻuwai ma ka lani.

column1: Feather softens the edge, so nobody sees the cut. Press + on feather.
column2: Hoʻopalupalu ʻo Feather i ka lihi, i ʻike ʻole kekahi i ka ʻoki. Kaomi i ka + ma feather.

column1: A hard edge says 'someone was here'. A soft one says nothing at all.
column2: ʻŌlelo ka lihi paʻakikī 'aia kekahi ma ʻaneʻi'. ʻAʻohe mea i ʻōlelo ʻia e ka lihi palupalu.

column1: A library shape, the pen, invert and feather. The Bureau thanks you. The Bureau was never here.
column2: He kinona waihona, ka peni, hoʻohuli a me ka hulu. Mahalo ke Keʻena iā ʻoe. ʻAʻole i hele mai ke Keʻena ma ʻaneʻi.

column1: Masks also go on a layer, an output, or its matte: MASK ON chooses. And every control takes a ~.
column2: Hele pū nā uhi ma kekahi papa, kekahi puka, a i ʻole kona matte: koho ʻo MASK ON. A lawe kēlā me kēia mana i ka ~.

column1: The truth is in the waveform, Hollis. Next time, the scopes.
column2: Aia ka ʻoiaʻiʻo ma ka waveform, Hollis. I ka manawa aʻe, nā scope.

column1: A lighthouse, a ghost, and a keeper who has been alone with the lamp far too long. Press START.
column2: He hale ipukukui, he lapu, a me ke kahu i noho hoʻokahi me ke kukui no ka manawa lōʻihi loa. Kaomi i START.

column1: Projection mapping: bending the picture to fit the building. Warp, blend, slices.
column2: Projection mapping: ke kekeʻe ʻana i ke kiʻi i kūpono i ka hale. Hoʻokekeʻe, hoʻohui, nā ʻāpana.

column1: Ye'll be wanting the ghost on the windows. Mind the lamp. The lamp is MINE.
column2: Makemake ʻoe i ka lapu ma nā puka aniani. Mālama i ke kukui. Naʻu ke kukui.
KE ANA ʻĀINA O KA PUKA

column1: MENU, then Video Outputs, then Geometry. Where an output's shape lives.
column2: PAPA KUHIKUHI, a laila Video Outputs, a laila Geometry. Kahi e noho ai ke kinona o ka puka.

column1: Geometry: the projector-menu word for 'what shape is the picture'.
column2: Geometry: ka huaʻōlelo papa kuhikuhi projector no 'he aha ke kinona o ke kiʻi'.

column1: Press warp edit, then drag a corner on the programme monitor. The window is not square. Neither is the keeper.
column2: Kaomi i warp edit, a laila kauo i ke kihi ma ka papakaumaka papahana. ʻAʻole huinahā like ka puka aniani. ʻAʻole pū ke kahu.

column1: A corner pin moves the four corners. Perspective keeps the lines straight, like a real window.
column2: Neʻe ka corner pin i nā kihi ʻehā. Mālama ʻo Perspective i nā laina pololei, e like me ka puka aniani maoli.

column1: LEFT! Ye call that a corner? I've seen straighter gulls.
column2: HEMA! He kihi kēlā iā ʻoe? Ua ʻike au i nā manu kai pololei aʻe.

column1: Back in Geometry: edge blend, + on the left and + on the right.
column2: Hoʻi i Geometry: edge blend, + ma ka hema a me + ma ka ʻākau.

column1: Two projectors overlap; each fades its edge so the overlap is not twice as bright.
column2: Kau ʻelua projector kekahi ma luna o kekahi; hoʻēmi kēlā me kēia i kona lihi i ʻaʻole pālua ka ʻōlinolino o ka wahi like.

column1: Geometry, SLICES, open. The Screens window is where slices are cut and placed.
column2: Geometry, SLICES, open. ʻO ka puka aniani Screens kahi e ʻoki ʻia ai a hoʻonoho ʻia ai nā ʻāpana.

column1: A slice is a piece of the picture, put anywhere on the output.
column2: He ʻāpana o ke kiʻi ka slice, kau ʻia ma nā wahi a pau o ka puka.

column1: In the Screens window, + SLICE three times, and drag each crop to a third of the picture.
column2: Ma ka puka aniani Screens, + SLICE ʻekolu manawa, a kauo i kēlā me kēia ʻoki i ka hapakolu o ke kiʻi.

column1: Three windows, three slices: left, middle and right of one picture.
column2: ʻEkolu puka aniani, ʻekolu ʻāpana: hema, waena a me ka ʻākau o ke kiʻi hoʻokahi.

column1: Three windows. The lamp gets the middle one. The lamp ALWAYS gets the middle one.
column2: ʻEkolu puka aniani. Loaʻa i ke kukui ka mea waena. Loaʻa MAU i ke kukui ka mea waena.

column1: Warp, blend, slices. The keeper will finally sleep. The gulls will not.
column2: Hoʻokekeʻe, hoʻohui, nā ʻāpana. E hiamoe ke kahu i ka hopena. ʻAʻole nā manu kai.

column1: Slices have their own warp and mesh in the Screens window. And a ~ on the place and the turn.
column2: He warp a me ka mesh ponoʻī ko nā ʻāpana ma ka puka aniani Screens. A he ~ ma ke kūlana a me ka huli.

column1: Ye did alright, lad. Now get away from the lamp.
column2: Ua maikaʻi kāu hana, keiki. I kēia manawa e haʻalele i ke kukui.

column1: A game show, skapi. Three contestants, one buzzer, and cues that fire from anywhere. Press START.
column2: He hōʻike pāʻani, skapi. ʻEkolu mea hoʻokūkū, hoʻokahi pele, a me nā cue e hoʻā mai nā wahi a pau. Kaomi i START.

column1: Cue numbers, hotkeys, and GO from other machines. Like a sequencer you can play from any key.
column2: Nā helu cue, nā kī wikiwiki, a me GO mai nā kamepiula ʻē aʻe. E like me ka sequencer hiki iā ʻoe ke hoʻokani mai kekahi kī.

column1: Welcome to the show! Let's spin that wheel!
column2: Welina mai i ka hōʻike! E wili kākou i ka huila!

column1: Contestant 3 is selected. In the inspector's metadata, give it a cue number: 3.
column2: Ua koho ʻia ka mea hoʻokūkū 3. Ma ka metadata o ka nānā cue, hāʻawi iā ia i ka helu cue: 3.

column1: Theatre numbers its cues. Q3, Q3.5, Q12A. Deckboy reads them all.
column2: Helu ka hale keaka i kona mau cue. Q3, Q3.5, Q12A. Heluhelu ʻo Deckboy iā lākou a pau.

column1: I'd like to buy a number, please.
column2: Makemake au e kūʻai i ka helu, e ʻoluʻolu.

column1: Ctrl+G, type the number, Enter. It goes live wherever the list happens to be standing.
column2: Ctrl+G, kikokiko i ka helu, Enter. Ola ia i kahi e kū ana ka papa helu.

column1: GOTO. The fastest way across a long list. Faster than scrolling. Much faster than me.
column2: GOTO. Ke ala wikiwiki loa ma kahi papa helu lōʻihi. Wikiwiki aʻe ma mua o ka ʻōwili. Wikiwiki loa ma mua oʻu.

column1: Contestant 1 is selected. In TRIGGERS, press key, then F5. That key now fires this cue.
column2: Ua koho ʻia ka mea hoʻokūkū 1. Ma TRIGGERS, kaomi i key, a laila F5. Hoʻā kēlā kī i kēia cue i kēia manawa.

column1: F1 to F10, F12, or the number pad. Each one, a buzzer.
column2: F1 a F10, F12, a i ʻole ka papa helu. Kēlā me kēia, he pele.
Loaʻa i kēlā me kēia mea hoʻokūkū he pele.

column1: Press the key. The cue fires, wherever the list is standing.
column2: Kaomi i ke kī. Hoʻā ka cue, i kahi e kū ana ka papa helu.

column1: No mouse, no list, no looking. Just the key.
column2: ʻAʻohe ʻiole, ʻaʻohe papa helu, ʻaʻohe nānā. ʻO ke kī wale nō.

column1: Companion, a MIDI note, an OSC message: MENU, then Network, says where each one connects.
column2: Companion, he note MIDI, he leka OSC: PAPA KUHIKUHI, a laila Network, haʻi i kahi e hoʻopili ai kēlā me kēia.

column1: A Stream Deck in the next room can press GO. So can a keyboard synth. I prefer the synth.
column2: Hiki i ka Stream Deck ma ka lumi aʻe ke kaomi i GO. Pēlā pū ka synth papa kī. Makemake au i ka synth.

column1: And for our viewers at home: you can play along too.
column2: A no kā mākou poʻe nānā ma ka home: hiki iā ʻoukou ke pāʻani pū.

column1: Numbers, GOTO, a buzzer, and GO from anywhere. You are a game show now, skapi.
column2: Nā helu, GOTO, he pele, a me GO mai nā wahi a pau. He hōʻike pāʻani ʻoe i kēia manawa, skapi.

column1: A cue can have a key, a MIDI note and an OSC address at once. Belt, braces and a second belt.
column2: Hiki i ka cue ke loaʻa he kī, he note MIDI a me ka helu wahi OSC i ka manawa hoʻokahi. Kāʻei, kaulawaha a me ke kāʻei ʻelua.
Aloha ahiahi, e nā mea a pau! E wili mau!

column1: Channel 6 weather, skapi. A map, a presenter, and a very large lizard. Press START.
column2: Ka ʻeā o ke Kahawai 6, skapi. He palapala ʻāina, he mea hōʻike, a me ka moʻo nui loa. Kaomi i START.

column1: Words on screen: Lower Thirds, text, and backdrops.
column2: Nā huaʻōlelo ma ka papakaumaka: nā Lower Third, ka huaʻōlelo, a me nā kua.

column1: I'm June O'Neil, and nothing about this forecast is normal.
column2: ʻO June O'Neil au, a ʻaʻohe mea maʻamau o kēia wānana.

column1: Words go on their own layer: press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Hele nā huaʻōlelo ma ko lākou papa ponoʻī: kaomi i ka + ma ka hopena o nā kāwele papa helu.

column1: A second playlist is a layer over the map. The lizard stays underneath. Mostly.
column2: He papa ma luna o ka palapala ʻāina ka papa helu ʻelua. Noho ka moʻo ma lalo. Ka hapa nui.

column1: Words on top. Always on top.
column2: Nā huaʻōlelo ma luna. Ma luna mau.

column1: In the new playlist: SOURCE, then Lower Third.
column2: Ma ka papa helu hou: SOURCE, a laila Lower Third.

column1: A name and a title, low on the screen, out of the lizard's way.
column2: He inoa a me ke kūlana, haʻahaʻa ma ka papakaumaka, ma waho o ke ala o ka moʻo.

column1: In the inspector, title: type the presenter's name. The second line is her job.
column2: Ma ka nānā cue, title: kikokiko i ka inoa o ka mea hōʻike. ʻO kāna hana ka lalani ʻelua.

column1: Spelling counts. The audience reads it at the speed of light.
column2: He koʻikoʻi ka pela ʻana. Heluhelu ka poʻe nānā me ka māmā o ka mālamalama.

column1: Spell it right. Last week it said 'Jane O'Meal'.
column2: E pela pololei. I kēlā pule aku ua ʻōlelo ʻia 'Jane O'Meal'.

column1: TAKE the Lower Third. Her name slides in over the map.
column2: TAKE i ka Lower Third. Paheʻe kona inoa ma luna o ka palapala ʻāina.

column1: Two layers live: the weather, and the words on top of it.
column2: ʻElua papa ola: ka ʻeā, a me nā huaʻōlelo ma luna.

column1: Thank you. Now, about that lizard...
column2: Mahalo. I kēia manawa, no kēlā moʻo...

column1: SOURCE, then Text: a title card. Then its backdrop chip: key green, for the vision mixer to key out.
column2: SOURCE, a laila Text: he kāleka poʻo inoa. A laila kona pahu kua: ʻōmaʻomaʻo kī, no ka mea hoʻohui kiʻi e kī ai.

column1: A backdrop fills behind the words. Key green or key blue, and the mixer does the rest.
column2: Hoʻopiha ke kua ma hope o nā huaʻōlelo. ʻŌmaʻomaʻo kī a polū kī paha, a hana ka mixer i ke koena.

column1: Breaking news: it's standing on the five-day forecast.
column2: Nūhou koʻikoʻi: ke kū nei ia ma luna o ka wānana ʻelima lā.

column1: A Lower Third, a name, a title card, a backdrop. The lizard has left the studio, skapi.
column2: He Lower Third, he inoa, he kāleka poʻo inoa, he kua. Ua haʻalele ka moʻo i ke keʻena, skapi.

column1: Lower Thirds can wait, slide and leave on their own. Their section has every setting.
column2: Hiki i nā Lower Third ke kali, paheʻe a haʻalele nona iho. Aia nā koho a pau ma ko lākou ʻāpana.

column1: That's the weather. Back to you, guys. Run.
column2: ʻO ia ka ʻeā. Hoʻi iā ʻoukou. Holo.

column1: A rocket built in a basement, skapi, and an inventor who wants cheese. Press START.
column2: He pōhaku ahi i kūkulu ʻia ma lalo o ka hale, skapi, a me ka mea hana makemake i ka waiū paʻa. Kaomi i START.

column1: Stage timers: countdowns, clocks, and a presenter view for the person on stage.
column2: Nā uaki kahua: nā helu i lalo, nā uaki, a me ka nānā o ka mea hōʻike no ke kanaka ma ke kahua.

column1: Cheese, Grommet! The moon's made of it. We'll need a countdown.
column2: Waiū paʻa, Grommet! Hana ʻia ka mahina me ia. Pono kākou i ka helu i lalo.

column1: SOURCE, then Stage Timer. A clock that counts down, in big friendly numbers.
column2: SOURCE, a laila Stage Timer. He uaki e helu i lalo, me nā helu nui ʻoluʻolu.

column1: Its colours change as it runs out: white, amber, red. Like a VU meter for time.
column2: Loli kona mau waihoʻoluʻu ke pau: keʻokeʻo, ʻākala, ʻulaʻula. E like me ka mika VU no ka manawa.

column1: Select the timer and TAKE it. The countdown starts.
column2: Koho i ka uaki a TAKE iā ia. Hoʻomaka ka helu i lalo.

column1: Past zero it keeps going, counting the overtime. Very honest. Slightly rude.
column2: Ma hala o ka ʻole holo mau ia, e helu ana i ka manawa keu. ʻOiaʻiʻo loa. ʻAʻole maikaʻi iki.

column1: Ten... nine... ooh, I do love a countdown.
column2: ʻUmi... iwa... ʻoh, aloha au i ka helu i lalo.

column1: Something's loose! Space holds the countdown. The clock shows it is held.
column2: Aia kekahi mea i wehe ʻia! Paʻa ʻo Space i ka helu i lalo. Hōʻike ka uaki ua paʻa ʻia.

column1: A hold is not a stop. Space again, and it carries on from where it was.
column2: ʻAʻole ka hoʻopaʻa he hoʻōki. Space hou, a hoʻomau ia mai kahi i waiho ai.
KA NĀNĀ O KA MEA HOʻOKELE

column1: MENU, Video Outputs: make an output's type PRESENTER. The person on stage gets the timer, the next cue and their notes.
column2: PAPA KUHIKUHI, Video Outputs: hoʻonoho i ke ʻano o ka puka i PRESENTER. Loaʻa i ke kanaka ma ke kahua ka uaki, ka cue aʻe a me kāna mau memo.

column1: A presenter view is an output like any other. Point it at the confidence monitor.
column2: He puka e like me nā mea ʻē aʻe ka nānā o ka mea hōʻike. Kuhikuhi iā ia i ka papakaumaka hilinaʻi.

column1: So the pilot can see the time. The pilot is Grommet.
column2: I ʻike ka mea hoʻokele i ka manawa. ʻO Grommet ka mea hoʻokele.

column1: A countdown, a hold, and a view for the pilot. Nazdrave, skapi. Bring crackers.
column2: He helu i lalo, he hoʻopaʻa, a me ka nānā no ka mea hoʻokele. Nazdrave, skapi. Lawe mai i nā pelena.

column1: Timers can also count up, or show the time of day. Their section has the lot.
column2: Hiki i nā uaki ke helu i luna, a hōʻike paha i ka hola o ka lā. Aia nā mea a pau ma ko lākou ʻāpana.

column1: A grand day out, Grommet! Pass the crackers.
column2: He lā nui ma waho, Grommet! Hāʻawi mai i nā pelena.

column1: A magic show, skapi. A trunk, a prop, and one beat where everything changes at once. Press START.
column2: He hōʻike kilokilo, skapi. He pahu, he mea hana, a me ka paʻi hoʻokahi e loli ai nā mea a pau. Kaomi i START.

column1: Two playlists are two layers. TAKE ALL changes both together.
column2: ʻElua papa helu he ʻelua papa. Hoʻololi ʻo TAKE ALL iā lāua ʻelua pū.

column1: Every trick needs two things happening at once. And a rubber chicken.
column2: Pono kēlā me kēia hana kilokilo i ʻelua mea i ka manawa hoʻokahi. A me ka moa lāpala.

column1: The prop goes on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Hele ka mea hana ma kona papa ponoʻī. Kaomi i ka + ma ka hopena o nā kāwele papa helu.

column1: Playlist 2 sits on top of playlist 1. Like a transparency on an overhead projector.
column2: Noho ka papa helu 2 ma luna o ka papa helu 1. E like me ka pepa akaka ma ka projector kahiko.

column1: Nothing up my sleeve. Everything in my trunk.
column2: ʻAʻohe mea i loko o koʻu lima kapa. Nā mea a pau i loko o kaʻu pahu.

column1: In the new playlist, add anything: PATTERN will do. That is the prop.
column2: Ma ka papa helu hou, hoʻohui i kekahi mea: maikaʻi ʻo PATTERN. ʻO ia ka mea hana.

column1: Whatever it is, it will appear the instant the trunk opens.
column2: He aha lā ia, e puka mai ia i ka wehe ʻana o ka pahu.

column1: Is it a rubber chicken? It's always a rubber chicken.
column2: He moa lāpala anei? He moa lāpala mau nō.

column1: Select 'The trunk (open)' in playlist 1 and the prop in playlist 2. Then TAKE ALL: both on one beat.
column2: Koho iā 'The trunk (open)' ma ka papa helu 1 a me ka mea hana ma ka papa helu 2. A laila TAKE ALL: ʻelua i ka paʻi hoʻokahi.

column1: One press, every playlist's selected cue. The audience never sees the seam.
column2: Hoʻokahi kaomi, ka cue i koho ʻia o kēlā me kēia papa helu. ʻAʻole loa ʻike ka poʻe nānā i ka humuhumu.
Ta-daaa! ...Kali no ka paʻipaʻi lima. Kali. Kali.

column1: Two layers, one beat. Every playlist has its own opacity and can sit on any output. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: ʻElua papa, hoʻokahi paʻi. He opacity ponoʻī ko kēlā me kēia papa helu a hiki ke noho ma kekahi puka. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: A magician never reveals. A playlist never minds being revealed.
column2: ʻAʻole hōʻike ka mea kilokilo. ʻAʻole hopohopo ka papa helu ke hōʻike ʻia.

column1: Thank you! I'm here all week! The chicken is here forever.
column2: Mahalo! Aia au ma ʻaneʻi i ka pule holoʻokoʻa! Aia ka moa ma ʻaneʻi mau loa.

column1: A cooking show, skapi. Live. Everything is on fire. Press START.
column2: He hōʻike kuke, skapi. Ola. Ke ʻā nei nā mea a pau. Kaomi i START.

column1: BLACK hides the picture and keeps the show running. PANIC stops everything. Know which you need.
column2: Hūnā ʻo BLACK i ke kiʻi a holo mau ka hōʻike. Hoʻōki ʻo PANIC i nā mea a pau. E ʻike i ka mea āu e pono ai.

column1: The audience must not see this. Press BLACK, or B.
column2: ʻAʻole pono ka poʻe nānā e ʻike i kēia. Kaomi i BLACK, a i ʻole B.

column1: The picture goes. The cue keeps playing underneath, ready to come back.
column2: Hala ke kiʻi. Holo mau ka cue ma lalo, mākaukau e hoʻi mai.

column1: The fire's out. Press B again: the picture comes back, still running.
column2: Ua pio ke ahi. Kaomi hou i ka B: hoʻi mai ke kiʻi, e holo mau ana.

column1: Nothing was lost. A mute on a mixer, for pictures.
column2: ʻAʻohe mea i nalo. He mute ma ka mixer, no nā kiʻi.

column1: Worse: MENU, System, the SAFETY card: PANIC. Everything stops, the way the panic setting says.
column2: ʻOi aku ka ʻino: PAPA KUHIKUHI, System, ke kāleka SAFETY: PANIC. Kū nā mea a pau, e like me ka ʻōlelo a ka hoʻonoho panic.

column1: PANIC is the big red button. Use it when BLACK is not enough. Then breathe.
column2: ʻO PANIC ka pihi ʻulaʻula nui. E hoʻohana inā ʻaʻole lawa ʻo BLACK. A laila e hanu.

column1: Close MENU, select the souffle, and TAKE it. The show is back on.
column2: Pani i ka PAPA KUHIKUHI, koho i ka souffle, a TAKE iā ia. Ua hoʻi ka hōʻike.

column1: After a panic, the show is still there. Pick up where you meant to be.
column2: Ma hope o ka panic, aia nō ka hōʻike. E hoʻomau ma kahi āu i manaʻo ai e hele.

column1: BLACK to hide, PANIC to stop, TAKE to come back. You will survive any kitchen, skapi.
column2: BLACK e hūnā, PANIC e hoʻōki, TAKE e hoʻi mai. E ola ana ʻoe ma kekahi lumi kuke, skapi.

column1: The panic setting chooses what PANIC does: fade out, cut, or just the outputs.
column2: Koho ka hoʻonoho panic i ka hana a PANIC: hala, ʻoki, a i ʻole nā puka wale nō.

column1: Presets, skapi. A whole look, remembered, and back with one button. Press START.
column2: Nā preset, skapi. He ʻano holoʻokoʻa, hoʻomanaʻo ʻia, a hoʻi mai me ka pihi hoʻokahi. Kaomi i START.

column1: Like the patch memory on a synth: store, then recall.
column2: E like me ka hoʻomanaʻo patch ma ka synth: mālama, a laila kiʻi hou.

column1: Press DASH: buttons of your own, for anything at all.
column2: Kaomi i DASH: nā pihi ponoʻī nou, no nā mea a pau.

column1: Ctrl+D also works. Very fast. Very professional.
column2: Hana pū ʻo Ctrl+D. Wikiwiki loa. Loea loa.

column1: Press +, then 'preset - a new preset from what is on now'. The button remembers this look.
column2: Kaomi i ka +, a laila 'preset - a new preset from what is on now'. Hoʻomanaʻo ka pihi i kēia ʻano.

column1: Store. Like saving the patch before the drummer leans on the synth.
column2: Mālama. E like me ka mālama ʻana i ka patch ma mua o ke kau ʻana o ka mea hoʻokani pahu ma luna o ka synth.
E HOʻOLOLI I NĀ MEA A PAU

column1: Close the DASH (Esc), then select Look two and TAKE it. A different look.
column2: Pani i ka DASH (Esc), a laila koho iā Look two a TAKE iā ia. He ʻano ʻē aʻe.

column1: Change it all. Don't worry. It remembers.
column2: Hoʻololi i nā mea a pau. Mai hopohopo. Hoʻomanaʻo ia.

column1: Open the DASH and press your preset button. The first look comes back.
column2: Wehe i ka DASH a kaomi i kāu pihi preset. Hoʻi mai ke ʻano mua.

column1: Recall. The patch memory, returning. Beautiful.
column2: Kiʻi hou. Ka hoʻomanaʻo patch, e hoʻi mai ana. Nani.

column1: A look, stored and recalled. A preset can keep cues, positions, effects, levels and routing; its button's menu chooses which.
column2: He ʻano, mālama ʻia a kiʻi hou ʻia. Hiki i ka preset ke mālama i nā cue, nā kūlana, nā hopena, nā pae a me ke ala; koho ka papa o kona pihi i nā mea.

column1: And a DASH button can run any command at all. Any. Even the exciting ones.
column2: A hiki i ka pihi DASH ke holo i kekahi kauoha. Kekahi. ʻOiai nā mea hoihoi.

column1: A space-opera trailer, skapi. A narrator with a very deep voice and opinions about transitions. Press START.
column2: He hōʻike mua kiʻiʻoniʻoni ākea, skapi. He mea haʻi moʻolelo me ka leo hohonu loa a me nā manaʻo e pili ana i nā hoʻololi. Kaomi i START.

column1: A transition is how one cue becomes the next. There are far more than the crossfade.
column2: ʻO ka hoʻololi ke ala e lilo ai kekahi cue i ka mea aʻe. Nui loa aʻe ma mua o ka crossfade.

column1: In a galaxy of content... one operator... must choose a transition.
column2: Ma kahi wahi hōkū o nā mea... hoʻokahi mea hoʻohana... pono e koho i ka hoʻololi.

column1: 'The planet' is selected. In the inspector, its transition style: choose iris.
column2: Ua koho ʻia 'The planet'. Ma ka nānā cue, kona ʻano hoʻololi: koho i iris.

column1: Pushes, wipes, iris, dip to white. Even a portal. I wrote half of them. On a Tuesday.
column2: Nā pahu, nā kāwele, iris, hāʻule i ke keʻokeʻo. ʻOiai he puka. Naʻu i kākau i ka hapa. I ka Pōʻalua.

column1: The planet deserves... a dramatic entrance.
column2: Pono ka honua i... ke komo ʻana koʻikoʻi.

column1: Give it a time: + on transition until it says a second or more.
column2: Hāʻawi iā ia i ka manawa: + ma transition a ʻōlelo ia i hoʻokahi kekona a ʻoi aku.

column1: No time, no transition. A style needs a duration to do anything at all.
column2: ʻAʻohe manawa, ʻaʻohe hoʻololi. Pono ke ʻano i ka lōʻihi e hana ai i kekahi mea.

column1: TAKE the planet. Watch it arrive.
column2: TAKE i ka honua. Nānā i kona hiki ʻana mai.

column1: The transition belongs to the cue arriving. Each cue chooses its own entrance.
column2: No ka cue e hiki mai ana ka hoʻololi. Koho kēlā me kēia cue i kona komo ʻana.

column1: Now 'The battle': choose shatter, give it a time, and TAKE it.
column2: I kēia manawa 'The battle': koho i shatter, hāʻawi i ka manawa, a TAKE iā ia.

column1: Shatter drops the old picture like a pane of glass. Please do not do this at a funeral.
column2: Hāʻule ʻo Shatter i ke kiʻi kahiko me he aniani lā. Mai hana i kēia ma ka hoʻolewa.

column1: A style, a time, and two very dramatic entrances. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: He ʻano, he manawa, a me ʻelua komo ʻana koʻikoʻi loa. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: A playlist has a default style too, for every cue that does not choose its own.
column2: He ʻano maʻamau ko ka papa helu pū, no kēlā me kēia cue ʻaʻole i koho i kona ʻano ponoʻī.

column1: Coming soon... to a desk near you.
column2: Ke hiki mai nei... i ka papa kokoke iā ʻoe.

column1: Two robot DJs, skapi. They do not talk. Their helmets do. Press START.
column2: ʻElua DJ lopako, skapi. ʻAʻole lāua e kamaʻilio. ʻO ko lāua mau pāpale kila ke kamaʻilio. Kaomi i START.

column1: Every cue has its own chain of audio effects, and some of them break the sound on purpose.
column2: He kaulahao hopena leo ponoʻī ko kēlā me kēia cue, a uhaki kekahi o lākou i ka leo me ka manaʻo.

column1: > HELLO. WE ARE HERE TO FIX YOUR MIX.
column2: > ALOHA. AIA MĀUA MA ʻANEʻI E HOʻOPONOPONO I KĀU MIX.

column1: The beat is selected. In its AUDIO EFFECTS section, + adds one. Try the delay.
column2: Ua koho ʻia ka paʻi. Ma kona ʻāpana AUDIO EFFECTS, hoʻohui ka + i hoʻokahi. E hoʻāʻo i ka delay.

column1: Delay, reverb, filters, a compressor. Amount always means 'less of this'.
column2: Delay, reverb, nā kānana, he compressor. ʻO ka nui ke ʻano 'emi iho o kēia'.

column1: > ONE MORE TIME. WITH ECHO. ECHO. ECHO.
column2: > HOʻOKAHI MANAWA HOU. ME KA LEO HOʻI. HOʻI. HOʻI.

column1: Add a second: a bend, like crush. It damages the sound the way a broken file would.
column2: Hoʻohui i ka lua: he kekeʻe, e like me crush. Hōʻino ia i ka leo e like me ka waihona haki.

column1: The bends are my favourite. Like a tape left in the sun. On purpose.
column2: ʻO nā kekeʻe kaʻu punahele. E like me ka lipine i waiho ʻia i ka lā. Me ka manaʻo.
> PAʻAKIKĪ AʻE. MAIKAʻI AʻE. KAKANI AʻE. LEO NUI AʻE.

column1: MENU, then Audio: where each playlist's sound goes, and the patch for named outputs.
column2: PAPA KUHIKUHI, a laila Audio: kahi e hele ai ka leo o kēlā me kēia papa helu, a me ka patch no nā puka i kapa ʻia.

column1: Speakers, monitors, an in-ear for the drummer. The patch sends each its own.
column2: Nā pahu leo, nā mea nānā, he pepeiao no ka mea hoʻokani pahu. Hoʻouna ka patch i kēlā me kēia kāna ponoʻī.

column1: > AROUND THE MIX. AROUND THE MIX. AROUND THE MIX.
column2: > A PUNI KA MIX. A PUNI KA MIX. A PUNI KA MIX.

column1: An effect, a bend and the patch. The robots approve, skapi. I think. Their faces are helmets.
column2: He hopena, he kekeʻe a me ka patch. ʻAe nā lopako, skapi. Manaʻo wau. He pāpale kila ko lāua mau maka.

column1: Every audio effect can follow a ~ too, even Motion. Wave at the delay. It's wonderful.
column2: Hiki i nā hopena leo a pau ke hahai i ka ~ pū, ʻoiai ʻo Motion. ʻAleʻale i ka delay. Nani loa.

column1: > THANK YOU. GOOD NIGHT. WE ARE ROBOTS.
column2: > MAHALO. ALOHA AHIAHI. HE LOPAKO MĀUA.
Ka ʻōlinolino ma ka ʻalihi lani (hōʻike #2)

column1: The Bureau again, skapi. A glow on the horizon, and two agents who disagree about it. Press START.
column2: Ke Keʻena hou, skapi. He ʻōlinolino ma ka ʻalihi lani, a me ʻelua ʻelele kūʻē no ia. Kaomi i START.

column1: The scopes measure a picture: brightness, colour, levels. Numbers, not opinions.
column2: Ana nā scope i ke kiʻi: ka ʻōlinolino, ka waihoʻoluʻu, nā pae. Nā helu, ʻaʻole nā manaʻo.

column1: It's them, Brandt. It's a craft. Look how it glows.
column2: ʻO lākou, Brandt. He moku. E nānā i kona ʻōlinolino.

column1: The scopes read only what really goes out, never a preview. Turn the output on: MENU, Video Outputs, OUTPUT OFF.
column2: Heluhelu nā scope i ka mea e puka maoli ana wale nō, ʻaʻole loa ka nānā mua. Hoʻā i ka puka: PAPA KUHIKUHI, Video Outputs, OUTPUT OFF.

column1: Measuring a scaled-down preview would be measuring a photocopy. We measure the original.
column2: ʻO ke ana ʻana i ka nānā mua liʻiliʻi he ana ʻana i ke kope. Ana mākou i ke kumu.

column1: Chain of evidence, Hollis. The real signal or nothing.
column2: Kaulahao hōʻike, Hollis. Ka hōʻailona maoli a i ʻole ʻaʻohe mea.

column1: Close MENU. Above the monitor, the PROGRAM button: press it until it says SCOPES or BOTH.
column2: Pani i ka PAPA KUHIKUHI. Ma luna o ka papakaumaka, ka pihi PROGRAM: kaomi a ʻōlelo ia SCOPES a i ʻole BOTH.

column1: Both shows the picture and its scopes side by side. Very civilised.
column2: Hōʻike ʻo Both i ke kiʻi a me kona mau scope ma ka ʻaoʻao. Noʻeau loa.

column1: Click the waveform to make it big. Bright things sit high, dark things low, left to right as in the picture.
column2: Kaomi i ka waveform e hoʻonui. Noho nā mea ʻōlinolino ma luna, nā mea pōʻeleʻele ma lalo, hema a ʻākau e like me ke kiʻi.

column1: The glow is that spike near the top. Very bright. Bright is not the same as alien.
column2: ʻO ka ʻōlinolino kēlā kiko kiʻekiʻe ma luna. ʻŌlinolino loa. ʻAʻole like ka ʻōlinolino me ke kanaka ʻē.

column1: Look at the peak. Nothing a streetlight couldn't do.
column2: E nānā i ka piko. ʻAʻohe mea hiki ʻole i ke kukui alanui.

column1: Click it again to go back, then click the vectorscope: colour round a circle. Saturated runs to the edge.
column2: Kaomi hou e hoʻi, a laila kaomi i ka vectorscope: ka waihoʻoluʻu a puni ka pōʻai. Holo ka mea ikaika i ka lihi.

column1: Magenta, far out by the rim. A strong colour. Strong is not illegal. Yet.
column2: Magenta, ma kahi mamao ma ka lihi. He waihoʻoluʻu ikaika. ʻAʻole kapu ka ikaika. ʻAʻole i kēia manawa.

column1: It's off the chart, Brandt! Literally off the chart!
column2: Ma waho o ka pakuhi, Brandt! Ma waho maoli o ka pakuhi!

column1: And false colour: red is clipped, yellow nearly. Is the glow red?
column2: A me ka waihoʻoluʻu wahaheʻe: ʻoki ʻia ka ʻulaʻula, kokoke ka melemele. He ʻulaʻula anei ka ʻōlinolino?

column1: Clipped means the brightest the signal can carry, and then some lost. Detail gone.
column2: ʻO ka ʻoki ʻia ka ʻōlinolino loa e hiki ai i ka hōʻailona ke lawe, a nalo kekahi. Ua hala nā kikoʻī.

column1: Red. Clipped. Not alien, Hollis. Just too bright. Case closed.
column2: ʻUlaʻula. ʻOki ʻia. ʻAʻole kanaka ʻē, Hollis. ʻŌlinolino loa wale nō. Ua pani ʻia ka hihia.

column1: Waveform, vectorscope, false colour. The scopes settled it, skapi. The agents did not.
column2: Waveform, vectorscope, waihoʻoluʻu wahaheʻe. Ua hoʻoholo nā scope, skapi. ʻAʻole nā ʻelele.

column1: SCOPES SOURCE reads any output, and the matrix can be 709 or 2020. For the curious.
column2: Heluhelu ʻo SCOPES SOURCE i kekahi puka, a hiki i ka matrix ke 709 a i ʻole 2020. No ka poʻe nīele.

column1: Too bright for a streetlight, Brandt. Too bright for anything. ...I want to believe.
column2: ʻŌlinolino loa no ke kukui alanui, Brandt. ʻŌlinolino loa no nā mea a pau. ...Makemake au e manaʻoʻiʻo.

column1: Pictures that leave by cable or network, skapi, not only a window on a screen. Press START.
column2: Nā kiʻi e haʻalele ma ke uea a i ʻole ka pūnaewele, skapi, ʻaʻole wale he puka aniani ma ka papakaumaka. Kaomi i START.

column1: NDI over the network, SDI from a DeckLink card, ST 2110 for broadcast plants.
column2: NDI ma ka pūnaewele, SDI mai ka kāleka DeckLink, ST 2110 no nā hale hoʻolele.

column1: MENU, Video Outputs, then Devices: every way an output can leave this computer.
column2: PAPA KUHIKUHI, Video Outputs, a laila Devices: nā ala a pau e haʻalele ai ka puka i kēia kamepiula.

column1: Each one says whether this machine can do it, and what it needs if not.
column2: Haʻi kēlā me kēia inā hiki i kēia mīkini ke hana, a me ka mea e pono ai inā ʻaʻole.

column1: If this computer has NDI, switch NDI SENDING on: the picture is on the network. If not, SHOW ME moves on.
column2: Inā he NDI ko kēia kamepiula, hoʻā i NDI SENDING: aia ke kiʻi ma ka pūnaewele. Inā ʻaʻole, neʻe ʻo SHOW ME i mua.

column1: NDI finds itself on the network. No cables, only a good switch and patience.
column2: Loaʻa ʻo NDI iā ia iho ma ka pūnaewele. ʻAʻohe uea, he switch maikaʻi a me ke ahonui wale nō.

column1: The output's own page has the rest: a DeckLink card's SDI, ST 2110 with NMOS, Spout and Syphon.
column2: Aia ke koena ma ka ʻaoʻao ponoʻī o ka puka: ka SDI o ka kāleka DeckLink, ST 2110 me NMOS, Spout a me Syphon.

column1: Every one is just an output. The show does not know or care how it leaves.
column2: He puka wale nō kēlā me kēia. ʻAʻole ʻike a mālama ka hōʻike i kona ala e haʻalele ai.
Deck 3: kekahi mea e neʻe ana

column1: The bridge of the starship Cathode, skapi. Four feeds, one main viewer, one mystery. Press START.
column2: Ka alahele o ka moku hōkū Cathode, skapi. ʻEhā kahe, hoʻokahi papakaumaka nui, hoʻokahi pohihihi. Kaomi i START.

column1: The multiview shows every playlist at once. Like a wall of oscilloscopes, but in space.
column2: Hōʻike ka nānā lehulehu i nā papa helu a pau i ka manawa hoʻokahi. E like me ka paia o nā oscilloscope, akā ma ka lewa.

column1: Frequencies open, Captain. All of them. That's the problem.
column2: Ua wehe ʻia nā alapine, Kāpena. Nā mea a pau. ʻO ia ka pilikia.

column1: MULTI, above the monitor: every playlist in its own window.
column2: MULTI, ma luna o ka papakaumaka: kēlā me kēia papa helu ma kona puka aniani ponoʻī.

column1: One window per playlist, the programme first.
column2: Hoʻokahi puka aniani no kēlā me kēia papa helu, ka papahana ma mua.

column1: Jinkys! Four feeds. And one of them has a monster in it.
column2: Jinkys! ʻEhā kahe. A he moʻo ʻino i loko o kekahi.

column1: Add a window (+), then its ... menu: make it show NEXT. What goes live when you press TAKE.
column2: Hoʻohui i ka puka aniani (+), a laila kona papa ...: e hōʻike iā NEXT. Ka mea e ola ke kaomi ʻoe i TAKE.

column1: Every window has a ... button. It chooses what that window shows.
column2: He pihi ... ko kēlā me kēia puka aniani. Koho ia i ka mea e hōʻike ai kēlā puka aniani.

column1: I need to see who's calling before they reach the main viewer.
column2: Pono au e ʻike i ka mea e kāhea mai ana ma mua o ko lākou hiki ʻana i ka papakaumaka nui.

column1: And one more window, showing the clock. Operators who watch a clock are never late. Mostly.
column2: A hoʻokahi puka aniani hou, e hōʻike ana i ka uaki. ʻAʻole lohi ka poʻe nānā i ka uaki. Ka hapa nui.

column1: Time of day, big. Stardates are just very long timecode.
column2: Ka hola o ka lā, nui. He timecode lōʻihi loa wale nō nā lā hōkū.

column1: The monster only shows up at midnight. We're going to need a clock.
column2: Puka mai ka moʻo ʻino i ke aumoe wale nō. Pono kākou i ka uaki.

column1: Any window's ... menu, then a layout: one big, the rest small.
column2: Ka papa ... o kekahi puka aniani, a laila he hoʻonohonoho: hoʻokahi nui, ke koena liʻiliʻi.

column1: The big window is window one. Usually the programme. Usually.
column2: ʻO ka puka aniani nui ka puka aniani ʻekahi. ʻO ka papahana ka hapa nui. Ka hapa nui.

column1: Main viewer big. The captain likes it big.
column2: Papakaumaka nui, nui. Makemake ke kāpena iā ia he nui.

column1: Select Deck 3 in playlist 3 and TAKE. Watch its window.
column2: Koho iā Deck 3 ma ka papa helu 3 a TAKE. Nānā i kona puka aniani.

column1: The red border is TALLY: the window that is on air. On screen, as they say on starships.
column2: ʻO ka lihi ʻulaʻula ka TALLY: ka puka aniani e ola ana. Ma ka papakaumaka, e like me kā lākou ʻōlelo ma nā moku hōkū.

column1: There! Feed three! Put it on screen!
column2: Aia! Kahe ʻekolu! Kau iā ia ma ka papakaumaka!

column1: Windows, the ... menu, NEXT, the clock, a layout, tally. Mystery solved, skapi.
column2: Nā puka aniani, ka papa ..., NEXT, ka uaki, he hoʻonohonoho, ka tally. Ua hoʻomaopopo ʻia ka pohihihi, skapi.

column1: A window can also show an output, with its warp and slices. Handy when it's a lighthouse.
column2: Hiki i ka puka aniani ke hōʻike i ka puka, me kona warp a me nā ʻāpana. Pono ke lilo ia i hale ipukukui.

column1: And the monster was... the ship's cook, all along. Jinkys.
column2: A ʻo ka moʻo ʻino... ʻo ka mea kuke o ka moku, mai ka hoʻomaka. Jinkys.

column1: finish or leave the lesson you are in first
column2: hoʻopau a haʻalele paha i ka haʻawina āu e noho nei ma mua

column1: Psst. It's me, the desk. I'll be watching. Supportively.
column2: Psst. ʻO wau, ka papa. E nānā ana au. Me ke kākoʻo.

column1: Hi! I'm the one doing all of this, by the way.
column2: Aloha! ʻO wau ka mea e hana nei i kēia mau mea a pau, ma ke ala.

column1: Ctrl+D opens the DASH. I'm just saying.
column2: Wehe ʻo Ctrl+D i ka DASH. Ke ʻōlelo wale nei au.

column1: Nearly there. I can feel it in my pixels.
column2: Kokoke. Ke ʻike nei au ma koʻu mau kiko.

column1: You're good at this. I can tell. I'm the one doing it.
column2: Akamai ʻoe ma kēia. Ke ʻike nei au. ʻO wau ka mea e hana nei.

column1: Every click, I heard. Every single one.
column2: Ua lohe au i kēlā me kēia kaomi. Kēlā me kēia.

column1: The glowing one. I can see it from here. It's glowing for you.
column2: Ka mea ʻōlinolino. ʻIke au iā ia mai ʻaneʻi. Ke ʻōlinolino nei nou.

column1: lesson paused - MENU > LESSONS picks up where you left off
column2: hoʻomaha ka haʻawina - hoʻomau ʻo PAPA KUHIKUHI > LESSONS ma kahi āu i waiho ai

column1: PROF. VIDEO:  The signal: what the picture is made of, and how to bend it. Pick a lesson.
column2: PROF. VIDEO:  Ka hōʻailona: ka mea i hana ʻia ai ke kiʻi, a me ke kekeʻe ʻana. Koho i haʻawina.

column1: DR. PIXEL:  Running the show, skapi. Fast hands, calm face. Pick a lesson.
column2: DR. PIXEL:  Ka holo ʻana i ka hōʻike, skapi. Lima wikiwiki, maka mālie. Koho i haʻawina.

column1: LESSONS  -  PART TWO  -  WHO DO YOU FOLLOW?
column2: NĀ HAʻAWINA  -  ʻĀPANA ʻELUA  -  ʻO WAI KĀU E HAHAI AI?
ka holo ʻana i ka hōʻike

column1: finish or leave LEARN THE BASICS first
column2: hoʻopau a haʻalele paha iā LEARN THE BASICS ma mua

column1: bug swat: Esc leaves, and your show comes back as it was
column2: bug swat: haʻalele ʻo Esc, a hoʻi kāu hōʻike e like me ia

column1: bug swat: your show is back. Motion's controls are in Settings > Audio
column2: bug swat: ua hoʻi kāu hōʻike. Aia nā mana Motion ma Settings > Audio

column1: Bugs are crawling to the cue list! Swat them by waving at your camera. First, Motion: in MOTION CONTROL turn it ON and choose what it READS.
column2: Ke kolo nei nā ʻelala i ka papa helu cue! Pāpaʻi iā lākou ma ka ʻaleʻale ʻana i kāu pahupaʻikiʻi. Ma mua, Motion: ma MOTION CONTROL hoʻā iā ia a koho i ka mea e HELUHELU ai.

column1: This one is NullPointer. Hollow, points at nothing. A finger goes straight through. Use the whole hand, skapi.
column2: ʻO NullPointer kēia. Puka, kuhikuhi i ka mea ʻole. Komo pololei ka manamana lima. E hoʻohana i ka lima holoʻokoʻa, skapi.

column1: Wave like you are hailing a cab! A small, polite cab. Not the buttons. The cab.
column2: ʻAleʻale me he mea lā e kāhea ana ʻoe i ke kaʻa hoʻolimalima! He kaʻa liʻiliʻi, ʻoluʻolu. ʻAʻole nā pihi. Ke kaʻa.

column1: Race Condition: twins, each sure it got there first. One reading cannot tell your hands apart, so drag two ZONES on the Motion picture, one each side.
column2: Race Condition: nā māhoe, manaʻo kēlā me kēia ua hiki mua ʻo ia. ʻAʻole hiki i ka heluhelu hoʻokahi ke ʻike i ka ʻokoʻa o kou mau lima, no laila kauo i ʻelua ZONES ma ke kiʻi Motion, hoʻokahi ma kēlā me kēia ʻaoʻao.

column1: Hit both together. Hit one, and they swap. Like my cousins at a wedding.
column2: Paʻi i lāua ʻelua pū. Paʻi i hoʻokahi, a hoʻololi lāua. E like me koʻu mau hoahānau ma ka male.

column1: One hand each side. Together! Together!
column2: Hoʻokahi lima ma kēlā me kēia ʻaoʻao. Pū! Pū!

column1: Off By One. The bug is not the face, it is the tiny extra segment, and a little wiggle needs a finer reading. Turn SENSITIVITY down to 5%.
column2: Off By One. ʻAʻole ka maka ka ʻelala, ʻo ka ʻāpana liʻiliʻi keu ia, a pono ka ʻoni liʻiliʻi i ka heluhelu nāwaliwali aʻe. Hoʻohaʻahaʻa iā SENSITIVITY i 5%.

column1: Lower number, finer reading. Yes, I also think it is backwards.
column2: Helu haʻahaʻa, heluhelu nāwaliwali. ʻAe, manaʻo pū wau ua hoʻohuli ʻia.

column1: Not the face. The little one on the end. Wiggle a finger.
column2: ʻAʻole ka maka. Ka mea liʻiliʻi ma ka hope. E hoʻoneʻe i ka manamana lima.

column1: Memory Leak. It only lets go while the reading stays up. Make FALL longer, 1.5 seconds or more, so your sweeps join up into one.
column2: Memory Leak. Hoʻokuʻu wale ia ke noho kiʻekiʻe ka heluhelu. E hoʻolōʻihi iā FALL, 1.5 kekona a ʻoi aku, i hui pū kāu mau kahili i hoʻokahi.

column1: Slow and steady, skapi. Like paying back a loan.

column1: Diamond is the hard-edged Atari Video Music lattice; rings tunnel well with feedback zoom.
column2: ʻO Diamond ka lattice Atari Video Music lihi paʻakikī; komo maikaʻi nā apo me ka hoʻonui hoʻihoʻi.

column1: Rock or spin. Depth 1 is half a turn either way; a saw at depth 1 turns it all the way round
column2: Luli a wili paha. ʻO ka hohonu 1 ka hapalua huli ma kēlā me kēia ʻaoʻao; huli ka saw ma ka hohonu 1 a puni

column1: DECK playback level (live, not saved with the cue) - per-cue trim is gain in the AUDIO section
column2: Pae hoʻokani PAPA (ola, ʻaʻole mālama ʻia me ka cue) - ʻo ka ʻoki cue ka ikaika ma ka ʻāpana AUDIO

column1: Still, fade in, typewriter, scroll up, crawl or pulse -- all driven by the cue's own transport
column2: Paʻa, hiki mai, mīkini kikokiko, ʻōwili i luna, kolo a panapana paha -- hoʻoholo ʻia e ka hoʻoholo ponoʻī o ka cue

column1: Fields per rendered frame. 1 is one for one, 0.5 holds each field for two frames, 0 freezes it.
column2: Nā kahua no ke kiʻi. ʻO 1 hoʻokahi no hoʻokahi, paʻa ʻo 0.5 i kēlā me kēia kahua no ʻelua kiʻi, hoʻopaʻa ʻo 0.

column1: What this cue shows while it plays: waveform, scope, Lissajous, spectrum, meters or a name card
column2: Ka mea a kēia cue e hōʻike ai ke hoʻokani: waveform, scope, Lissajous, spectrum, nā mika a i ʻole kāleka inoa

column1: 0 picks tiles by brightness so the picture reads. 1 picks at random so the grid becomes texture.
column2: Koho ʻo 0 i nā tile ma ka ʻōlinolino i heluhelu ʻia ke kiʻi. Koho wale ʻo 1 i lilo ka papa kōnane i ʻili.

column1: How far it travels, in semitones. Up reads as arrival, down as departure, zero is a struck note.
column2: Ka mamao o kona hele ʻana, ma nā semitone. Hiki mai ka piʻi, haʻalele ka iho, he note i paʻi ʻia ka ʻole.

column1: An IPv4 address. Names are not resolved: a DNS lookup is a blocking call and GO must not make one
column2: He helu wahi IPv4. ʻAʻole hoʻoholo ʻia nā inoa: kāohi ka nīnau DNS, a ʻaʻole pono ʻo GO e hana i kekahi

column1: Tile width in pixels. Must match the sheet's grid or the slices land across neighbouring sprites.
column2: Ākea tile ma nā pika. Pono e kūlike me ka papa kōnane o ka pepa, a i ʻole pae nā ʻāpana ma nā sprite e pili ana.

column1: Alternating mirrors by cell position, which reads as pattern where random flipping reads as noise.
column2: Nā aniani e kaʻahele ma ke kūlana pahu, heluhelu ʻia he kāpoʻe kahi e heluhelu ʻia ai ka huli wale he ʻuʻina.

column1: 0 welds them to their cell, which reads as engraved. Above it they re-roll, which reads as boiling.
column2: Hoʻopili ʻo 0 iā lākou i ko lākou pahu, heluhelu ʻia ua kālai ʻia. Ma luna aʻe ʻōwili hou lākou, heluhelu ʻia e paila ana.

column1: --- -- --  does nothing on that playlist  -  (M) the step's own playlist
column2: --- -- --  ʻaʻohe hana ma kēlā papa helu  -  (M) ka papa helu ponoʻī o ke kaʻina

column1: MONO L plays the left input in both speakers: mic 1 on most interfaces. STEREO is for a line source.
column2: Hoʻokani ʻo MONO L i ka komo hema ma nā pahu leo ʻelua: mic 1 ma ka hapa nui o nā mea hoʻopili. No ke kumu laina ʻo STEREO.

column1: The whole gesture. This IS the cue's duration -- a sting is the one generated signal here that ends.
column2: Ke ʻano holoʻokoʻa. ʻO kēia KA lōʻihi o ka cue -- ʻo ka sting ka hōʻailona hoʻokahi i hana ʻia ma ʻaneʻi e pau ana.

column1: Click the value to send this fixture or leave it where the last cue put it. ~ makes the level breathe
column2: Kaomi i ka helu e hoʻouna i kēia kukui a i ʻole waiho iā ia ma kahi a ka cue hope i kau ai. Hoʻohanu ʻo ~ i ka pae

column1: FDS is a wavetable bent by a modulator. 2A03 is the pulse/triangle/noise set most chiptune is made of.
column2: He papa nalu ʻo FDS i kekeʻe ʻia e ka modulator. ʻO 2A03 ka hui pulse/triangle/noise i hana ʻia ai ka hapa nui o ka chiptune.

column1: Scramble which glyph means which brightness. Same set, different handwriting. Seeded, so it stays put.
column2: Hoʻohuikau i ka hua e kuhikuhi ai i ka ʻōlinolino. Ka hui like, kākau lima ʻokoʻa. Hoʻopaʻa ʻia ka hua, no laila noho mau.

column1: Pixel sort: runs of pixels sorted by brightness within a row, which is what makes datamosh look melted.
column2: Hoʻonohonoho pika: nā pika i hoʻonohonoho ʻia ma ka ʻōlinolino i loko o ka lalani, ʻo ia ka mea e hehee ai ka datamosh.

column1: How many cells the marks may climb. They thin out as they go, so a tall reach trails rather than doubles.
column2: Ka nui o nā pahu e hiki ai i nā kaha ke piʻi. Lahilahi lākou ke hele, no laila hahai ka hōʻea kiʻekiʻe ma kahi o ka pālua.

column1: cue act val  -  G take  S stop  F fade out (val = tenths of a second)  V volume  O opacity  J jump to row
column2: cue hana helu  -  G lawe  S kū  F hala aku (helu = hapaʻumi kekona)  V leo  O ʻike ʻia  J lele i ka lalani

column1: Harmonic weight: a pure chime at zero, brass at full. This is the difference between a ping and a fanfare.
column2: Kaumaha harmonic: he kani maʻemaʻe ma ka ʻole, he keleawe ma ka piha. ʻO kēia ka ʻokoʻa ma waena o ka ping a me ka fanfare.

column1: Steps through the inputs this computer has. 'Settings input' follows the input chosen in Settings > Audio.
column2: Hele ma nā komo o kēia kamepiula. Hahai ʻo 'Settings input' i ka komo i koho ʻia ma Settings > Audio.

column1: Embers to roaring. It still surges and settles at any setting -- a fire that does not move reads as a photo
column2: Mai nā lānahu a i ka uwō. Piʻi a noho mau nō ia ma nā hoʻonoho a pau -- heluhelu ʻia ke ahi neʻe ʻole he kiʻi paʻi.

column1: Reference pitch. 440 is modern standard, 432 the common alternative, and older instruments sat lower still.
column2: Leo kiʻekiʻe kuhikuhi. ʻO 440 ka maʻamau hou, ʻo 432 ka mea ʻē aʻe maʻamau, a ua noho haʻahaʻa aʻe nā mea kani kahiko.

column1: Where the sting starts. Under a voice it wants to stay out of the way; over a room it wants to cut through.
column2: Kahi e hoʻomaka ai ka sting. Ma lalo o ka leo makemake ia e noho ma waho o ke ala; ma luna o ka lumi makemake ia e ʻoki.

column1: Digital gain on the input, -40 to +40 dB. Set the interface's own preamp first; this is for the last few dB.
column2: Ikaika kikohoʻe ma ka komo, -40 a +40 dB. Hoʻonoho mua i ka preamp ponoʻī o ka mea hoʻopili; no nā dB hope kēia.

column1: Pulse the size. On its own this moves width AND height together; give height its own ~ to squash and stretch
column2: Panapana i ka nui. Iā ia iho neʻe kēia i ke ākea A ME ke kiʻekiʻe pū; hāʻawi i ke kiʻekiʻe i kona ~ ponoʻī e kaomi a kīkoʻo

column1: A card fills the frame; a Lower Third is a name and a role, low on a transparent frame, with an in and an out
column2: Hoʻopiha ke kāleka i ke kiʻi; he inoa a me ke kūlana ka Lower Third, haʻahaʻa ma ke kiʻi akaka, me ke komo a me ka puka

column1: Held keeps the last displacement rather than removing it -- the picture stays bent the way the driver left it.
column2: Mālama ʻo Held i ka neʻe hope ma kahi o ka wehe ʻana -- noho ke kiʻi i kekeʻe ʻia e like me ka waiho ʻana a ka mea hoʻokele.

column1: --- -- --  does nothing on that playlist  -  (M) the step's own playlist  -  EDIT is on: typing changes the show
column2: --- -- --  ʻaʻohe hana ma kēlā papa helu  -  (M) ka papa helu ponoʻī o ke kaʻina  -  Ua hoʻā ʻia ʻo EDIT: hoʻololi ke kikokiko ʻana i ka hōʻike

column1: 12.5 and 25 are thin and reedy, 50 is hollow. 75 sounds identical to 25 -- it is here because trackers expose it.
column2: Lahilahi a mānoanoa ʻole ʻo 12.5 a me 25, puka ʻo 50. Like ka leo o 75 me 25 -- aia ma ʻaneʻi no ka mea hōʻike nā tracker iā ia.

column1: Quantise the output like the hardware. The steps ARE the sound; smoothing them makes it a synth imitating a chip.
column2: Hoʻokaʻawale i ka puka e like me ka mea hana. ʻO nā kaʻina KA leo; ʻo ka hoʻomālie ʻana iā lākou he synth e hoʻohālike ana i ka chip.

column1: Moves every selected cue's trim by the same dB, keeping the differences between them; typing a value sets them all to it
column2: Hoʻoneʻe i ka ʻoki o nā cue i koho ʻia ma ka dB like, me ka mālama ʻana i ko lākou ʻokoʻa; hoʻonoho ke kikokiko ʻana i ka helu iā lākou a pau

column1: Where the playlist's crosspoints send it (Settings > Audio). Click to open the matrix by name, starting from exactly that
column2: Kahi e hoʻouna ai nā kea o ka papa helu (Settings > Audio). Kaomi e wehe i ka matrix ma ka inoa, e hoʻomaka ana mai ia ala pololei

column1: Put back what it started from once the ramp lands (after the stop): a deck left ready for its next cue, a swell that lets go
column2: Hoʻihoʻi i kona hoʻomaka ʻana ke pae ka piʻina (ma hope o ke kū): he papa mākaukau no kona cue aʻe, he piʻi e hoʻokuʻu

column1: Which speech model makes the captions: English, any language, or the slower, more accurate pair. Each is a one-time download
column2: Ke kumu ʻōlelo e hana ai i nā huaʻōlelo: Pelekānia, kekahi ʻōlelo, a i ʻole ka pālua lohi aʻe, pololei aʻe. Hoʻoiho hoʻokahi manawa kēlā me kēia

column1: What the mask cuts: this cue wherever it plays, this playlist on the focused output, that output's whole picture, or its matte
column2: Ka mea a ka uhi e ʻoki ai: kēia cue ma nā wahi a pau e hoʻokani ai, kēia papa helu ma ka puka i kālele ʻia, ke kiʻi holoʻokoʻa o kēlā puka, a i ʻole kona matte

column1: Play at the screen's rate when it is within 0.2% (59.94 on 60): every frame shown once, the sound up to 3.5 cents sharp or flat
column2: Hoʻokani ma ka māmā o ka papakaumaka ke loko o 0.2% (59.94 ma 60): hōʻike ʻia kēlā me kēia kiʻi hoʻokahi manawa, ka leo a hiki i 3.5 cents kiʻekiʻe a haʻahaʻa

column1: Quarter turns are exact and stay crisp. Spinning samples at an angle, which tears pixel art -- sometimes that is what you want.
column2: Pololei nā huli hapahā a noho ʻoʻoleʻa. Laʻana ka wili ʻana ma ka huina, e haehae ana i ke kiʻi pika -- i kekahi manawa ʻo ia kāu e makemake ai.

column1: Every take starts the puppetry the same way, so a rehearsed look repeats instead of depending on how long the app has been open.
column2: Hoʻomaka kēlā me kēia lawe i ka hoʻoneʻe ma ke ala like, i hana hou ʻia ke ʻano i hoʻomaʻamaʻa ʻia ma kahi o ka pili ʻana i ka lōʻihi o ka wehe ʻana o ka app.

column1: What aims each tilt: its own position, the picture's luma gradient so characters lean the way the image does, or the cell's hue.
column2: Ka mea e kuhikuhi ai i kēlā me kēia hiō: kona kūlana ponoʻī, ka luma gradient o ke kiʻi i hiō nā hua e like me ke kiʻi, a i ʻole ke ʻano waihoʻoluʻu o ka pahu.

column1: Name a channel or a pair once. Playlists send to the name, so a different interface means changing the names here, not every cue.
column2: Kapa i ke kahawai a i ʻole ka pālua hoʻokahi manawa. Hoʻouna nā papa helu i ka inoa, no laila ʻo ka mea hoʻopili ʻokoʻa ka hoʻololi ʻana i nā inoa ma ʻaneʻi, ʻaʻole kēlā me kēia cue.

column1: Click a crosspoint to walk it: off, 0, -3, -6, -12 dB. Drag it sideways for any level. A playlist with none plays to its own device.
column2: Kaomi i ke kea e hele: pio, 0, -3, -6, -12 dB. Kauo iā ia ma ka ʻaoʻao no kekahi pae. Hoʻokani ka papa helu ʻaʻohe ona i kona mea hana ponoʻī.

column1: Sprite sets installed in data/sprites. Each folder there is a set; cycling picks one and wraps back to none. Right-click turns them off.
column2: Nā hui sprite i hoʻokomo ʻia ma data/sprites. He hui kēlā me kēia waihona ma laila; koho ka hoʻololi ʻana i hoʻokahi a hoʻi i ka ʻaʻohe. Hoʻopio ke kaomi ʻākau iā lākou.

column1: Internal resolution, 1 chunkiest to 5 finest. This is an aesthetic control as much as a speed one -- the 8-bit look comes from big pixels.
column2: Kikoʻī kūloko, 1 nui loa a 5 liʻiliʻi loa. He mana nani kēia e like me ka māmā -- mai nā pika nui mai ke ʻano 8-bit.

column1: Picture takes colour from the image. Green, amber and cyan are terminal phosphors. Palette locks the text to the selected hardware palette.
column2: Lawe ʻo Picture i ka waihoʻoluʻu mai ke kiʻi. He phosphor pahu kauoha ka ʻōmaʻomaʻo, ʻākala a me ka cyan. Hoʻopaʻa ʻo Palette i ka huaʻōlelo i ka papa waihoʻoluʻu mea hana i koho ʻia.

column1: SUBTLE self-heals (H.264). CLASSIC is the real smear (MPEG-4). EXTREME is chunkier and smears constantly. Changing this re-prepares the cue.
column2: Hoʻōla iā ia iho ʻo SUBTLE (H.264). ʻO CLASSIC ka hamo maoli (MPEG-4). Poloka aʻe ʻo EXTREME a hamo mau. Hoʻomākaukau hou ka hoʻololi ʻana i kēia i ka cue.

column1: Sine for line-up, pink to ring out a PA, white to find rattles, sweep to hear where a room rings, identify to walk the outputs one at a time.
column2: Sine no ka hoʻonohonoho, pink e hoʻokani i ka PA, keʻokeʻo e ʻimi i nā ʻuʻina, sweep e lohe i kahi e kani ai ka lumi, identify e hele ma nā puka i kēlā me kēia manawa.

column1: Which effect, by its place in the stack of the cue that deck is playing when this fires. With nothing there, the fade says so and does nothing
column2: Ka hopena, ma kona wahi i ka hōʻuluʻulu o ka cue e hoʻokani ana kēlā papa ke hoʻā kēia. Inā ʻaʻohe mea ma laila, haʻi ka hala a hana ʻole

column1: Each frame blended into the next. This is the Hypno signature -- at 0 it is a pattern generator, above it the picture starts feeding on itself.
column2: Hui ʻia kēlā me kēia kiʻi i ka mea aʻe. ʻO kēia ka hōʻailona Hypno -- ma ka 0 he mea hana kāpoʻe ia, ma luna aʻe hoʻomaka ke kiʻi e ʻai iā ia iho.

column1: What is through the window on the hearth wall: a garden, rain, snow or the sea. A room with weather outside reads as somewhere rather than as a wall
column2: Ka mea ma waho o ka puka aniani ma ka paia kapuahi: he māla, he ua, he hau a i ʻole ke kai. ʻO ka lumi me ka ʻeā ma waho, he wahi ia ma kahi o ka paia

column1: BY FIXTURE: the lights in the patch (Settings > Network > FIXTURES), by name. CHANNELS: channel=level by hand. A cue can carry both; channels go last
column2: MA KA KUKUI: nā kukui ma ka patch (Settings > Network > FIXTURES), ma ka inoa. NĀ KAHAWAI: kahawai=pae ma ka lima. Hiki i ka cue ke lawe i nā mea ʻelua; hope loa nā kahawai

column1: Each character rocks as though it were a card being tilted. Every cell has its own phase, so the grid breathes instead of sliding about as one sheet.
column2: Luli kēlā me kēia hua me he kāleka lā e hiō ana. He pae ponoʻī ko kēlā me kēia pahu, no laila hanu ka papa kōnane ma kahi o ka paheʻe ʻana me he pepa hoʻokahi lā.

column1: Pen: click for corners, drag for curves, click the first point to close (P). Points: drag, click the outline to add one, Alt-click or Delete to remove
column2: Peni: kaomi no nā kihi, kauo no nā pihi, kaomi i ke kiko mua e pani (P). Nā kiko: kauo, kaomi i ka laina waho e hoʻohui, Alt-kaomi a Delete paha e wehe

column1: The chip's three channels. They differ in kind: triangle has no volume control on the hardware, and noise is a shift register rather than an oscillator.
column2: Nā kahawai ʻekolu o ka chip. ʻOkoʻa ko lākou ʻano: ʻaʻohe mana leo o ka triangle ma ka mea hana, a he shift register ka noise ma kahi o ka oscillator.

column1: Curated sets of symbols and emoji -- stars, notes, flowers, arrows, weather, runes, faces. Picking one fills the custom glyphs below, which stays editable.
column2: Nā hui hōʻailona a me nā emoji i koho ʻia -- nā hōkū, nā note, nā pua, nā pua kuhikuhi, ka ʻeā, nā rune, nā maka. Hoʻopiha ke koho ʻana i nā hua ponoʻī ma lalo, hiki mau ke hoʻoponopono ʻia.

column1: Play from the computer keyboard, Ableton layout: A W S E D F T G Y H U J, Z and X for octave. While this is ON those keys make notes instead of firing cues.
column2: Hoʻokani mai ka papa kī kamepiula, ʻano Ableton: A W S E D F T G Y H U J, Z a me X no ka octave. Ke HOʻĀ kēia hana kēlā mau kī i nā note ma kahi o ka hoʻā ʻana i nā cue.

column1: Deck opacity, deck volume, the master dimmer, the active cue's own brightness / contrast / saturation / hue, or a knob of one of its effects or audio effects
column2: ʻIke ʻia o ka papa, leo o ka papa, ka hoʻēmi haku, ka ʻōlinolino / ʻokoʻa / ikaika waihoʻoluʻu / ʻano waihoʻoluʻu ponoʻī o ka cue ola, a i ʻole ka pihi o kekahi o kāna mau hopena a hopena leo paha

column1: Scanlines, phosphor bloom and RGB fringing. The bloom is the part that matters -- a phosphor spills sideways, which is why a CRT looks like it is emitting light.
column2: Nā laina scan, ka mohala phosphor a me ka lihi RGB. ʻO ka mohala ka ʻāpana koʻikoʻi -- kahe ka phosphor ma ka ʻaoʻao, no laila me he mea lā e hoʻopuka ana ka CRT i ka mālamalama.

column1: Torn scanline bands and RGB separation. In text mode it also corrupts CELLS -- whole rows lock to one repeating character, the way a real text screen loses sync.
column2: Nā kaola laina scan i haehae ʻia a me ka hoʻokaʻawale RGB. Ma ke ʻano huaʻōlelo hōʻino pū ia i nā PAHU -- paʻa nā lalani holoʻokoʻa i hoʻokahi hua hana hou, e like me ka nalo ʻana o ke kūlike o ka papakaumaka huaʻōlelo maoli.

column1: Still holds the frame you are on. Flipbook plays the frames in turn. Replay draws the first frame stroke by stroke, the way it was drawn, then holds and starts again
column2: Paʻa ʻo Still i ke kiʻi āu e noho nei. Hoʻokani ʻo Flipbook i nā kiʻi ma ka hulina. Kaha hou ʻo Replay i ke kiʻi mua kaha ma ke kaha, e like me kona kaha ʻia ʻana, a laila paʻa a hoʻomaka hou

column1: Start, Stop, Pause, Resume, Load (stand it by without firing), Arm, Disarm, or Devamp it (a loop plays out its pass and ends); or Stop all, Pause all, Resume all: every deck
column2: Start, Stop, Pause, Resume, Load (hoʻomākaukau me ka hoʻā ʻole), Arm, Disarm, a i ʻole Devamp (pau ka pōʻai i kona puni a pau); a i ʻole Stop all, Pause all, Resume all: nā papa a pau

column1: Scope shows shape and clipping. Lissajous shows phase and polarity between the first two channels -- a diagonal the wrong way means one is inverted. Spectrum is third-octave bars.
column2: Hōʻike ʻo Scope i ke kinona a me ka ʻoki. Hōʻike ʻo Lissajous i ka pae a me ka polarity ma waena o nā kahawai mua ʻelua -- ʻo ka diagonal ma ka ʻaoʻao hewa ka mea i hoʻohuli ʻia. He hapakolu octave ka Spectrum

column1: 0 picks the glyph the brightness asks for, 1 picks any glyph in the set. Turn it up to see the whole alphabet: ranked strictly by ink, a flat area picks one mark and the rest never appear.
column2: Koho ʻo 0 i ka hua a ka ʻōlinolino e noi ai, koho ʻo 1 i kekahi hua ma ka hui. Hoʻonui iā ia e ʻike i ka pīʻāpā holoʻokoʻa: ma ka ʻīnika wale nō, koho ka wahi pālahalaha i hoʻokahi kaha

column1: Blocks and dithers read as density; the ASCII ramp reads as text; symbols read as wreckage. Cycling this clears a custom glyph string, since that would override it -- the preset row puts one back.
column2: Heluhelu ʻia nā poloka a me nā dither he mānoanoa; heluhelu ʻia ka ramp ASCII he huaʻōlelo; heluhelu ʻia nā hōʻailona he ʻōpala. Holoi ka hoʻololi ʻana i kēia i nā hua ponoʻī, no ka mea e hoʻopau ia iā ia

column1: Equal temperament buys free modulation at the cost of every interval being slightly wrong. Just and pythagorean are exactly in tune in one key. Bohlen-Pierce divides a twelfth, so it has no octaves.
column2: Kūʻai ka equal temperament i ka modulation manuahi me ka hewa iki o kēlā me kēia interval. Kūlike pololei ʻo Just a me pythagorean ma hoʻokahi kī. Māhele ʻo Bohlen-Pierce

column1: load a sprite sheet from a file...
column2: hoʻouka i ka pepa sprite mai ka waihona...

column1: What fires this cue besides GO
column2: Ka mea e hoʻā ai i kēia cue ma waho o GO
Pocket Test (napoʻo ʻana o ka lā)
Palapala ʻāina papa (nā helu tile LED)
Puka (nā pōpō o ka lewa hohonu)
Aloha, e ke kanaka kahiko. Hoʻoleʻaleʻa kāu "slideshow" iā mākou.

column1: the words this cue puts on screen  |  Shift+Enter: new line  |  Enter: apply
column2: nā huaʻōlelo a kēia cue e kau ai ma ka papakaumaka  |  Shift+Enter: laina hou  |  Enter: hoʻohana

column1: name values with  d = ...;  end with one expression, or three for red green blue  |  Shift+Enter: new line  |  Enter: apply
column2: kapa i nā helu me  d = ...;  hoʻopau me hoʻokahi ʻōlelo, a ʻekolu paha no ka ʻulaʻula ʻōmaʻomaʻo polū  |  Shift+Enter: laina hou  |  Enter: hoʻohana

column1: Now click its tab, Deck 2. A new playlist is not the selected one until you click it.
